youtube.description: Attention, Nigerian tenants! Did you know there’s a new federal law that allows your rent payments to reduce your taxable income? From January 1, 2026, the Nigeria Tax Act of 2025 introduces a rent relief of 20% of your annual rent, capped at ₦500,000. This Deep-Dive explains exactly what this means for you, who can claim it, the essential documents you need, and how to declare your rent to benefit from this significant tax saving. Don't miss out on this opportunity to lighten your financial burden. Watch now to understand the process and prepare your documents. claims.text: s.30(2)(a)(vi) Nigeria Tax Act 2025 (in force 1 January 2026): in computing the taxable income of an individual, a rent relief of 20% of the annual rent paid, subject to a maximum of ₦500,000, is deducted — provided the individual accurately declares the actual amount of rent paid and other relevant information the relevant tax authority prescribes.
Rent relief replaces the Consolidated Relief Allowance of the Personal Income Tax Act from the 2026 year of assessment; a person who pays no rent has no rent relief.

The relief is claimed, not given: with no declaration the deduction is ₦0. An employee declares to the employer, who applies it through PAYE from the month the evidence is submitted; a self-employed person or anyone outside PAYE claims it in the annual return to the State tax authority (the Nigeria Revenue Service for FCT residents and others it assesses).

Joint Revenue Board PIT Guidelines 2026, para 9.6 — minimum information for rent relief: (i) the legal tenant's name; (ii) actual rent paid and the period covered; (iii) the landlord's full name and one of mobile number, Tax ID or NIN; (iv) the property address. A receipt in the tenant's own name with all four, the signed agreement and proof of payment is what HR and tax offices ask for.
Employer's annual PAYE return for the 2026 year: 31 January 2027. Individual annual return for 2026: 31 March 2027. Rent that straddles two years is apportioned to each.

Worked figures: ₦1,200,000 rent → ₦240,000 relief; ₦1,500,000 → ₦300,000; ₦2,500,000 or more → the ₦500,000 cap. The relief reduces taxable income, not the tax bill: the naira saved is the relief multiplied by the person's top rate.

Fourth Schedule, Nigeria Tax Act 2025 — rates on taxable income from 2026: 0% on the first ₦800,000; 15% on the next ₦2,200,000; 18% on the next ₦9,000,000; 21% on the next ₦13,000,000; 23% on the next ₦25,000,000; 25% above ₦50,000,000.

Joint Revenue Board PIT Guidelines 2026, paras 9.3–9.5: in a shared tenancy each tenant claims up to ₦500,000 on the portion of rent they bear; the relief is on an actual-year basis (rent paid in 2026 relieves 2026); rent spanning years is apportioned — the Board's own example: ₦2,000,000 for 24 months counts ₦1,000,000 for 2026, relief ₦200,000.
